summary: Karl Friedrich Keil worked in religious studies. He studied at Saint Peter's School, the University of Tartu under Samuel Gottlieb Rudolf Henzi (1827–1830), and Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp (~1831–1833), later serving as professor at Tartu (1838–1858).

Karl Friedrich Neumann worked in sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Heidelberg, Göttingen under Arnold Heeren, Munich, San Lazzaro degli Armeni, and under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat. He served as professor at the University of Munich (1833–1852) and Bavarian State Library curator (~1833–1863).
Karl G. Heider studied at Williams College (~1952–1954), Harvard College (~1954–1956), and Harvard University (~1957–1966).

Karl Georg Zistl was an Indologist who studied at the University of Munich under Ernst Kuhn (~1904–1908). From 1911 to 1952, he worked as a wissenschaftlicher Hilfsarbeiter at the Munich University Library.
Karl Gottlieb Ewald Rhenius was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the Berlin Mission Seminary in 1810 and served as a missionary for the Church Mission Society from ~1814 to 1835.

Karl Graul worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied theology at the University of Leipzig in 1834, directed the Leipzig Evangelical Lutheran Mission (1844–1860), and taught Missionswissenschaft at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg from 1861.

Karl H. Potter was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of California and Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, and held professorships at the University of Minnesota (~1956–1971) and the University of Washington (~1971–1997).

Karl Hoffmann specialized in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Munich under Walther Wüst, Hanns Oertel, and Ferdinand Sommer, and held chairs at Saarland University (1952–1955) and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (1955–1983).

Karl Hummel was a scholar in Indology who studied at Munich under Wilhelm Geiger (~1925–1928) and Tübingen under Enno Littmann (~1928–1933). He spent his career at Tübingen as an assistant and director (1946–1976), also visiting the University of Tehran.

Karl Jahn worked in Iranian/Central Asian studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Charles University under Moriz Winternitz and at Leipzig. He taught at the German University in Prague, Utrecht University (1950–1972), Leiden University (1953–1973), Istanbul University, and Vienna.
Karl Jaspers was a philosopher who studied at Heidelberg University from ~1902 to 1908 and later held a post there from ~1909 to 1948.

Karl Jettmar worked in history/archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at Vienna under Robert Bleichsteiner and Robert von Heine-Geldern, later holding posts at the Weltmuseum Wien, University of Vienna, Mainz, and Heidelberg University (1964–1986).

Karl Joseph Hieronymus Windischmann worked in philosophy and Indology. He studied at the University of Mainz and the University of Würzburg, later holding professorships at Lyceum and Gymnasium Aschaffenburg (from 1803) and the University of Bonn (from 1818).

Karl Lachmann worked in linguistics. He studied at the University of Leipzig (~1809–1812) and the University of Göttingen (~1812–1815), and served as a professor at Humboldt University of Berlin from ~1825 to 1851.

Karl Marx was a philosopher who studied at Gymnasium Friedrich Wilhelm, Bonn (under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker), Humboldt University of Berlin, and Jena. He held posts at the Rheinische Zeitung (~1842–1843) and the Neue Rheinische Zeitung (~1848–1849).

Karl Müllenhoff worked in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at the Meldorfer Gelehrtenschule, Kiel University, Humboldt University of Berlin, and Leipzig University. He held academic posts at Kiel University (from 1842) and Frederick William University Berlin (from 1858).

Karl Otfried Müller worked in history/archaeology and linguistics. He studied at Breslau and Berlin under August Boeckh, Friedrich Schleiermacher, and Friedrich August Wolf. He taught at Magdalenaeum Wrocław and served as professor at the University of Göttingen from 1819.

Karl Popper was a philosopher who studied at the University of Vienna and the University of Cambridge. He held academic posts at the University of Canterbury (1937–1945), London School of Economics, King's College London, and the University of London (1949–1969).

Karl Reinhardt worked in philosophy. He studied at Bonn and Berlin under Ulrich von Wilamowitz-Moellendorff, and held posts at the universities of Bonn (~1914–1919), Hamburg (~1919–1923), Frankfurt (~1924–1942), and Leipzig (~1942–1946).

Karl Richard Lepsius worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig, Göttingen, and Berlin under August Boeckh. His career included leadership roles at the DAI Rome, Humboldt University of Berlin, Egyptian Museum of Berlin, and Prussian State Library.
